text:
oncall-bot: [PAGER] high error rate detected on /v1/generate — 504s spiking to 20% for NA-hosted pool. Alert threshold hit at 2025-03-10T01:20:30Z. Paging alex chen and the SRE rotation.

alex chen: ack, I'm on. pulling logs now. quick question: is this across all models or one endpoint?

maria gonzalez: seeing same in metrics. errors concentrated on requests targeting model: gpt-open-7b-quant. latency up too.

alex chen: starting live tail: `kubectl logs --selector=service=inference -f --since=15m` 

sre-ops-bot: NOTE: autoscaler triggered 2x in last 10m due to request concurrency.

alex chen: logs show repeated timeouts to the kv-cache backend, 502/timeout at 10s. Rolling a quick config to bypass cache for affected route to see if perf improves.

jordan lee: if cache is the culprit, fallback to no-cache should reduce tail latencies. need someone to watch capacity while we do this.

alex chen: executing change: PATCH /routes/generate -> set cache_policy="bypass" (deploying config)...

sre-ops-bot: config deploy started (deploy-id: cfg-20250310-01).

alex chen: after patch: error rate dropped from 20% -> 6% within 60s. Latency reduced by ~300ms p50. Looks like cache service instability.

maria gonzalez: confirm, error spikes correlate with elevated error responses from cache host pool. I'll open a ticket on infra side.

support-bot: note: two customer support tickets opened referencing delays/failed requests starting ~01:19Z. Ticket IDs: SUP-9342, SUP-9343.

alex chen: marking immediate mitigation as successful. Creating short-lived runbook to avoid autoscaler oscillation while infra fixes cache pool.

jordan lee: agree we should schedule a controlled rollback to original config once cache is healthy; need to avoid traffic surge to cache.

alex chen: handing off to jordan for next 2-hour watch. Summary: bypassed cache on /v1/generate, reduced 504s to 6%, opened infra ticket for cache hosts (INFRA-5777).

jordan lee: ack takeover. I'll keep watch and coordinate with INFRA.

--- post-incident coordination (10:45Z) ---

diane wang: good job. we need to lock in next steps: postmortem owner, timeline, customer communications. propose PM owner = alex, postmortem meeting Wed 2025-03-12 16:00 UTC. anyone object?

alex chen: I can own the writeup. I'll collect timeline + logs.

sam patel: I'll draft a status page update and a customer email template once we have RCA. Suggest we proactively offer affected customers a follow-up call.

maria gonzalez: infra will patch cache host health-check and rotate the pool. ETA for full remediation ~6 hours from now. I'll add remediation tasks to INFRA ticket.

support-bot: customers impacted (based on error traces): account_42, account_99, account_enterprise_7. We'll queue proactive outreach once copy ready.

alex chen: scheduling: postmortem doc created: https://docs.redwood.ai/postmortems/1854321000 — I'll fill initial timeline and actions. Meeting invite sent to SRE, INFRA, Product, Support.

--- draft status page copy (sam patel) ---

sam patel: DRAFT (Status page):

```
Incident 2025-03-10 — Increased 504 errors for text generation endpoint
Summary: We experienced elevated 504 errors affecting a subset of requests to our text generation API between 01:19Z and 01:42Z. Impact: Intermittent failures and increased latency for some customers. Mitigation: We disabled a caching layer for the affected route to restore success rates. Current status: Partial mitigation complete; full remediation in progress. Next update: within 4 hours or when remediation completes. Contact: support@redwood.ai
```

sam patel: planning to post an initial Status Page update referencing incident link once QA approves.

diane wang: keep language clear on what happened and what customers should expect. Include a link to request a follow-up call.

--- action items captured in thread ---

alex chen: ACTION-1: Postmortem writeup + timeline + logs. Owner: alex chen. Due: 2025-03-12 08:00 UTC (doc draft).

maria gonzalez: ACTION-2: Infra remediation — replace unhealthy cache hosts, add stricter health-checks, and add alert to catch similar kv-cache timeouts. Owner: maria gonzalez / infra team. Due: 2025-03-10 12:00 UTC. Ticket: INFRA-5777.

jordan lee: ACTION-3: Follow-up watch and rollback plan if re-enabled. Owner: jordan lee. Due: ongoing for next 24h.

sam patel: ACTION-4: Draft customer communication (status page + email + call offer). Owner: sam patel + support. Due: 2025-03-10 10:30 UTC.

diane wang: ACTION-5: Exec summary and customer outreach strategy for top 3 impacted accounts. Owner: diane wang. Due: 2025-03-10 11:30 UTC.

--- customer outreach plan ---

sam patel: Proposed email template (short):

```
Hi <Customer>,
We experienced intermittent failures impacting some text generation requests on 2025-03-10 between ~01:19Z and ~01:42Z. We mitigated the issue by bypassing a caching layer which restored success rates. We're still performing a full remediation and will share a detailed RCA when complete. If you'd like a dedicated call to review impact on your usage, please reply and we'll schedule.

Apologies for the disruption — Sam, Support Team, Redwood Inference
```

support-bot: queued outreach to account_42 and account_enterprise_7. Manual review required before sending.

--- reputation & trust recovery steps ---

diane wang: propose the following trust rebuild steps:
- proactive 1:1 calls with top impacted enterprise customers within 48h.
- produce a technical RCA with mitigation and timeline and publish on docs site.
- offer one week of usage credit for affected accounts as a gesture (support to confirm).
- run a follow-up health-check report after infra remediation and share with customers.

sam patel: agree. I'll draft the credit policy and legal can approve.

alex chen: technical note for RCA: root cause appears to be intermittent failure/latency in the kv-cache tier causing upstream timeouts; autoscaler amplifies the effect by adding more traffic during spikes. We'll include logs, graphs, and the config diff in the doc.

maria gonzalez: adding action: add saturation-based autoscaler guardrails to avoid feedback loops. ACTION-6: Autoscaler guardrails. Owner: maria gonzalez. Due: 2025-03-17 18:00 UTC.

--- scheduling & next steps ---

diane wang: Postmortem meeting set: 2025-03-12 16:00 UTC (invite includes SRE, INFRA, Product, Support, Solutions Eng). Please prepare: timeline, logs, customer impact summary, and proposed remediation plan.

alex chen: will attach initial timeline and the `curl` logs + stack traces to the doc by end of day.

sam patel: I'll post the initial status page update at 09:00Z once copy is approved by Diane.

jordan lee: leaving a note: if we re-enable cache, do a canary with 1% traffic and slow ramp.

--- closing notes (12:30Z) ---

alex chen: thanks everyone. handing final ownership of customer comms to sam and exec summary to diane. I'll finalize the technical RCA draft.

diane wang: thanks team, appreciate quick mitigation and clear ownership. We'll track progress in the postmortem doc and update customers once RCA is final. :thumbsup:

support-bot: Incident closed for page rotation at 2025-03-10T12:28:00Z — monitoring mode enabled.

oncall-bot: Reminder: postmortem template / checklist: https://docs.redwood.ai/playbooks/postmortem-template

end of thread: brief follow-ups expected in the postmortem doc and during the scheduled meeting.
